title: Study your energy
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What are the first ten things you do when you wake up?

Jose said that in the last two or three pages of the chapter the book gives five points, and he wanted to practice them on the call. He asked students: what are the first ten things you do when you wake up?
A student said: I go through my to-do list in bed, take a cold shower, get ready, make breakfast, and read while I make it. Then I join the stand-up call and my day starts.
Jose said the further you get into your day, the more critical the steps become, because they involve people and your focus. Studying your energy level is very important.

I don't do business calls after three in the afternoon, he said, because my energy is already going down. I get up at four every morning. If I have very important meetings, I line them up the day before for the peak of my energy.

A student said what happens after lunch is a bit more brain fog. Jose said: if you are in a negotiation, you must be careful. Maybe push your lunch to two o'clock and do a little fasting so your energy doesn't drop.

The ups and the troughs will influence your decision-making, and somebody else's too, he said. He said sports agents negotiate for six, seven, eight hours and must be physically fit, hydrating like athletes.

groups.heading: Too much of a good thing

lines.text: Jose said he loves coffee in the morning but you can go overboard. Once in a while do a cleanse, because after a while you get tolerant, and caffeine can give you a lot of anxiety. If you already have anxiety about something and add caffeine, it can make you almost irrational. All of it is a balance.
When is your peak, and what is on your calendar then?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the first ten things you do when you wake up.
Write the hours when your energy peaks.
Write what is on your calendar in those hours.
Write what you do to avoid a drop after lunch.

check.q: What did Jose say to line up for your peak energy?
choices: The most important calls and meetings

check.q: What did a student say happens after lunch?
What did Jose say about caffeine?
choices: You can go overboard; it is a balance

recap: Know your energy cycle. Put important things at your peak.
